extraction_text: Ambarisha used force to seize the kingdom when evil people prevailed and good people suffered.

attributes.reason: To combat evil and protect the good

extraction_text: Ambarisha punished evil, promoted good deeds, achieved great success, and chanted verses about governance.
Ambarisha identified greed as the remaining evil that traps people in desire and leads to suffering and rebirth.

attributes.insight: Greed is the root cause of suffering and rebirth
attributes.solution: Cut off greed with the arrow of wisdom

extraction_text: Ambarisha emphasized self-control and self-rule as the true form of kingship.
King Janaka tried to expel a Brahmin who violated scriptures from his domain.

attributes.conflict: King attempts to enforce scriptural law

extraction_text: The Brahmin asked King Janaka to define the boundaries of his domain so he could leave.

attributes.response: Brahmin agrees to obey but needs clarity

extraction_text: King Janaka became distressed and unable to answer when confronted with defining his domain.
After contemplation, King Janaka realized he either has no domain or everything is his domain.

attributes.realization: Domain is either nonexistent or universal
attributes.philosophical_insight: Questioning the nature of kingship and territory

extraction_text: Janaka declares that even his body is not his own, or that the entire earth is his, and tells the other person to live and enjoy wherever they wish.
The other person asks Janaka by what wisdom he has overcome selfishness, and by what wisdom he claims everything as his domain while also claiming to have no domain.

attributes.action: Asking for explanation of Janaka's wisdom

extraction_text: Janaka explains that he knows all things have beginnings and ends, so he doesn't know what can be called his own. He cites the Vedas questioning ownership.

Janaka describes how he has conquered the elements by not desiring sensory objects: earth through smell, water through taste, light through sight, wind through touch, sound through hearing, and mind through thoughts.

attributes.supernatural_elements: Control over natural elements through spiritual discipline

extraction_text: Janaka states that all his actions are for the gods, ancestors, all beings, and guests.

attributes.action: Describing the orientation of his actions

extraction_text: The Brahmin reveals himself as Dharma (the god of righteousness) who came to test Janaka.
Dharma declares Janaka to be a Chakravartin (universal monarch) with Brahman as the hub, wisdom as the spokes, and goodness as the rim that never reverses.
The text is identified as Chapter 32 of the Ashvamedha Parva in the Mahabharata.
